questions.title: Why does the partition function vanish in the Bradley‑Terry re‑parameterization of DPO?
questions.question_body: In equation (6) of the DPO paper the partition function $Z(x)$ seems to disappear when deriving the human preference probability in terms of the optimal policy $ oldsymbol{	heta}$. I understand that substituting the log‑ratio form from equation (5) into the BT model makes $Z(x)$ cancel, but I am not entirely convinced how this algebraic cancellation works when we have two different completions $y_1$ and $y_2$. Could you explain step‑by‑step why $ rac{1}{1+ rac{Z(y_2)}{Z(y_1)}}$ simplifies to a logistic of the log‑ratios of $ rac{ oldsymbol{	heta}(y_n ig|x)}{ oldsymbol{	ext{ref}}(y_n ig|x)}$?

questions.title:
What exactly is being optimized when we use the loss 
$  oxed{	extstyle- eta igl(
abla_	heta 	anh(r_{	heta}(x,y_w)-r_{	heta}(x,y_l)) igr)
}$ in DPO?
questions.question_body:
Equation (7) gives a gradient expression that contains terms like $
abla_{	heta}	anh(r_{	heta}(x,y_w)-r_{	heta}(x,y_l))$. The paper says this weight is higher when the implicit reward mis‑orders the two completions. However, I never saw a 	anh term in the original DPO objective; it looks like a variant. Is this a typo, or is there an alternative DPO formulation that uses tanh? How does this relate to standard binary cross‑entropy?

questions.title: Does DPO require any form of reward scaling or normalization?
questions.question_body: The traditional RLHF pipeline often normalizes reward values to have zero mean so that equivalence classes do not distort learning. In DPO we bypass explicit rewards, yet we still compute an implicit reward as $r_	heta(x,y)= eta igl(	extstyle	ext{log} rac{ oldsymbol{	heta}(y|x)}{ oldsymbol{m ref}(y|x)} igr)$. Does this implicit reward suffer from scale ambiguities? If so, how does DPO ensure a comparable scale to what is achieved after reward normalisation in standard RLHF?

questions.title: How do we choose $ eta$ in practice and what does it reflect about model conservativeness?
questions.question_body: The paper lists several experiments where $ eta$ is swept over $ igl ackslash{0.05,0.10,1.0,5.0 igr}$ and mentions that it controls how much the policy can deviate from $ oldsymbol{m ref}$. Yet I cannot find an analytical relation between $ eta$ and expected KL divergence or temperature‐like scaling in policy iteration. Is there a principled way—e.g., through a Lagrange multiplier analysis—to set $ eta$ for a target average KL divergence?

questions.title: Can we interpret DPO as a special case of ‘control as inference’?
questions.question_body: Equation (12) shows an objective where we penalise ${ f r} -  eta	extstyle	ext{log} rac{}{}$ which looks similar to entropy regularised MDPs. In section 4.1 you mention control as inference with follow–up normalisation terms. Is there a mathematical one–to–one mapping between DPO’s closed‑form policy and standard soft–policy methods (e.g., soft‑RL with KL projection)? How does that impact variance during training compared to PPO?
